summary: Describes the WITHIN extension to IMAP SEARCH, with OLDER and YOUNGER keys that take an interval rather than a date. It helps devices with limited capacity or bandwidth that use persistent searches. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5032 adds IMAP search keys for finding messages older or younger than a time interval. The server calculates the cutoff using its current time and each message's internal date.

questions: imap older and younger search keys
how to search imap mail by age
what are imap older and younger search keys
subtitle: Two IMAP search keys that match mail by its age in seconds.

tldr.problem: Clients that perform persistent searches may waste bandwidth and processing by repeatedly asking for messages within a changing date range.
tldr.mechanism: The WITHIN extension adds OLDER and YOUNGER search keys that compare each message's internal date with the server's current time minus a supplied interval.
tldr.outcome: The extension supports interval-based searches and can reduce repeated requests, but dynamic search results may be delayed.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 5032's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC updates RFC 3501 with the WITHIN search extension.

sections.title: Search by a Time Interval
sections.content:
IMAP's BEFORE and SINCE keys compare message dates with a date supplied by the client. WITHIN adds OLDER and YOUNGER keys that instead take a non-zero interval in seconds.

The RFC describes this as useful for persistent searches when a device cannot search regularly or a network has limited bandwidth and repeated requests would create extra traffic.
sections.plainLanguage: A client can ask for messages based on how long ago they arrived. It gives an interval rather than calculating and sending a calendar date.

sections.title: How OLDER and YOUNGER Match
sections.content:
The server subtracts the interval from its current date and time to calculate a target time. OLDER matches messages whose internal date is at or before that target; YOUNGER matches messages whose internal date is at or after it.

The server must advertise the WITHIN capability. The comparison is exact to the resolution of a second.
sections.plainLanguage: The server works out a cutoff from its own clock. OLDER finds messages on or before it, and YOUNGER finds messages on or after it.

sections.title: Dynamic Searches May Lag
sections.content:
A server may evaluate a dynamic search periodically rather than after every mailbox change. As a result, the search results can lag behind the current mailbox state.

If a client needs a result that reflects the mailbox at the moment of the request, the RFC recommends issuing a new search.
sections.plainLanguage: A persistent search may not show a new message immediately. The client can run another search when it needs an up-to-date result.
